title: They looked alive.
paragraphs:
You can fool a crowd…
but you cannot fool Christ.
Here’s the tension we don’t want to admit:

What if the most dangerous place to be spiritually dead…
is inside the church?

What if the applause is loud…
but the Spirit is silent?

What if everything looks right…
but something eternal is missing?
Jesus didn’t whisper this to Sardis.

“I know your works. You have a reputation for being alive, but you are dead.”
— Revelation 3:1
Because this wasn’t a scandalous church on the outside.

No headlines of immorality.
No public collapse.
No obvious rebellion.
A slow, silent death behind a polished reputation.

Not in obvious sin…
but in spiritual performance.
You start believing your own image.
This is the deception of Sardis:
Looking alive becomes a substitute for being alive.

“I’m doing fine.”
“I’m not like them.”
“I know enough.”
“I’ve been in church for years.”
But Scripture cuts through that illusion:

“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
— James 4:6

Not because He hates you—
but because pride keeps you from the very grace that can save you.
But He’s no longer at the center.

“Wake up, and strengthen what remains and is about to die…”
— Revelation 3:2
Because dead things don’t wake themselves up.
Some of us don’t need more sermons.
Some of us don’t need better routines.
Because no amount of activity can replace intimacy with Christ.
No reputation can replace a surrendered heart.
Here’s the truth we must face:
You can be surrounded by worship… and still be far from God.

“This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.”
— Matthew 15:8
Jesus did not walk away from Sardis.
If you feel exposed right now…
Because the same Jesus who spoke to Sardis…
Is the same Jesus who stood at a tomb and cried out:
Because Jesus doesn’t just diagnose death.

“And you were dead in the trespasses and sins… but God, being rich in mercy… made us alive together with Christ.”
— Ephesians 2:1,4–5
And His resurrection offers you something religion never can—
So what do you do now?

Are you alive in Christ…
or just maintaining an image?

Are you walking with Jesus…
or just familiar with Him?

Are you surrendered…
or just surrounded by Christian culture?
but to let shame lead you to redemption.
Because the cross already absorbed your guilt.
If pride has quietly taken over—
If you’ve been “looking alive” but feel empty inside—
Jesus is not asking for your image.

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
